A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SATBench research. All 14 pages of v1 and 18 pages of v2, including figures, tables, equations, references, and appendices, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original model prediction and reasoning-trace results in Tables 3–4, difficulty analyses, and human validation of 100 examples.

after.justification: V2 retains original benchmark evaluations and reports additional error distributions, direct-formula evaluations, prompting interventions, and fine-tuning results.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 and Figure 1 replace agreement of original and reconstructed SAT/UNSAT labels with logical-equivalence checking through bidirectional entailment. This substantially strengthens the stated dataset-acceptance procedure. Section 6.2 also introduces error-aware prompting and LoRA adaptation, while the underlying puzzle-generation and trace-evaluation framework remains.

E1.justification: V2 adds evaluation directly on CNF formulas alongside narrative puzzles (Section 6.1, Table 6), introducing a symbolic-input scenario. The core 2100-puzzle benchmark and Boolean-satisfiability task coverage remain; no additional language or broader reasoning domain is evaluated.

E2.justification: The main comparison drops Mixtral-8x7B and Mixtral-8x22B from Table 3 and the Mixtral series from Figure 3. The other main models and five-model trace comparison are retained. Section 6.2 adds an untuned-versus-LoRA-tuned Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct comparison.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce GPT-4o error classification, direct-CNF testing, error-aware re-prompting restricted to previously misclassified cases, and LoRA fine-tuning on 1100 correct o4-mini traces. These substantially expand the evaluation design beyond the retained zero-shot benchmark, whose difficulty bins and accuracy metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's scaling, difficulty, trace-quality, and human-validation analyses, v2 adds four-category error distributions for o4-mini and DeepSeek-R1 (Table 5), representative paraphrased failures (Appendix C), a narrative-versus-formula comparison (Table 6), and prompting/fine-tuning interventions targeting performance weaknesses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated experimental runs, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates. The added error-frequency percentages are additional point results, not a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 2–4 contain revised statistics and scores: o4-mini overall accuracy changes from 89.4% to 89.3%, and DeepSeek-R1 overall trace accuracy from 76.2% to 78.0%. V2 adds error distributions, formula-input scores, failure-correction rates of 60.4% and 73.2%, and LoRA accuracy of 51.9% versus 53.6%. Changed validation and dataset statistics prevent treating all cross-version score changes as same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 introduces the formal requirement that A and B are equivalent exactly when each entails the other, replacing the previous satisfiability-status comparison. This changes the mathematical validation condition. The CNF definitions and worked UNSAT derivation are retained, with no substantial new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The central claims about automated, difficulty-controlled SAT puzzles and weaknesses in LLM reasoning remain. V2 adds systematic failure categories to the abstract, contribution list, and conclusion, and introduces prompting/fine-tuning improvement efforts in the introduction, extending the analysis contribution.

C2.justification: V2 qualifies v1's positive scaling interpretation with plateaus on hard instances and adds explanations involving context inconsistency, omitted constraints, spurious priors, and backtracking failures. Section 6 interprets narrative inputs as adding reasoning complexity and discusses improvement interventions. The existing limitations concerning LLM-generated errors and Boolean-only coverage remain.

D1.justification: V2 newly supplies a code/data repository link and the full LLM consistency-validation prompt (Appendix B.1). It specifies uniform sampling, three independent co-author annotators, and majority voting for the retained 100-puzzle review, plus the model, adaptation technique, and training-trace source for LoRA. The annotation details are new disclosures, not evidence of additional validation runs.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations to FineReason, Faith and Fate, and Tyagi et al.'s grid-puzzle reasoning study. Section 2 more explicitly distinguishes SATBench from PARAT's formula inputs and AutoLogi's corpus-based generation and potential contamination. The broader related-work coverage and benchmark comparison remain.

P1.justification: V2 edits the abstract, introduction, contribution statements, and selected result interpretations; expands human-validation exposition; adds a Discussion section; and reorganizes the appendices into examples, templates, and error cases. Author/contact information and acknowledgments also change. Much of the existing method and experimental-setup prose is retained.

P2.justification: V2 adds Tables 5–6 and Figures A1–A2, redraws Figure 1's validation block, and revises Figure 3's series and legend. Figures 2 and 4 move, and the original split appendix prompt boxes become separately captioned Figures A3–A5 on individual pages. Those three prompt figures redisplay existing material rather than introduce three new procedures.

improvement.justification: The stronger equivalence check, validation prompt, annotation details, and code/data access information improve methodological clarity and reproducibility; the error analysis adds useful diagnosis. These gains are tempered by underspecified evaluation details for the new interventions and unreconciled scores: Table 6 gives o4-mini puzzle accuracy as 89.4%, matching v1 rather than v2's 89.3% in Table 3. The evidence supports a limited net improvement.
